Before giving your opinion about Morocco, you should obviously do a little research first. Step one: open a book about Moroccan history. Yes, an actual book with pages, because apparently watching a few TikToks is not enough to become an expert on an entire country. Start by learning about the Amazigh people, whose presence in North Africa goes back thousands of years. Learn about the different Amazigh communities in Morocco, their historical regions, languages, cultures, and traditions. You can look into groups such as the Rifains in the Rif, the Chleuhs in the Souss and southern regions, Amazigh communities of the Middle Atlas, and many others throughout the country. Because, surprisingly, “Amazigh” does not describe one single identical population living in one exact place. Then study Moroccan history before the Arab and Islamic periods: ancient North African populations, Phoenician and Carthaginian influences, the Roman period, and the different dynasties and political changes that shaped Morocco over time. After that, learn about the spread of Arabic language and culture, as well as the migrations, exchanges, and mixing of populations that happened throughout North African history. Then comes everyone’s favorite part: genetics. This is where you should actually read scientific studies instead of looking at one DNA chart on TikTok and suddenly deciding that you have discovered the complete genetic history of an entire population. Moroccan populations have a complex genetic history, with a major ancient North African component alongside influences from different populations that moved through and interacted with North Africa throughout history. Results can also vary between regions and populations, so maybe don’t take one study about one specific group and use it as the universal answer for every Moroccan. You should also learn the difference between ancestry, culture, language, identity, and genetics, because they are not the same thing. Speaking Arabic does not automatically mean having exactly the same genetic ancestry as every other Arabic-speaking person, just as being Amazigh does not mean belonging to one genetically identical population. Human history is, unfortunately for anyone looking for an easy answer, a little more complicated than a “choose your ethnicity” quiz. Then research Amazigh languages in Morocco, their history and official status, as well as the cultural diversity between different Moroccan regions. Learn how Amazigh, Arab, Moroccan, regional, and family identities can sometimes overlap rather than simply cancel each other out. Finally, after studying all of that, you might actually be ready to talk about Morocco without reducing thousands of years of history to two sentences you found online. If you genuinely want to understand Moroccan origins, you have to look at history, archaeology, languages, migrations, culture, and genetics together. There you go. You can officially begin your studies on Morocco now. Good luck with the curriculum. It’s slightly more complicated than expected. #morocco#aespa#ningning#ⵣ🇲🇦 #aespa
